results.basis: The 2025 Alberta Linear Property Assessment Minister's Guidelines define 'AER means the Alberta Energy Regulator' and then read assessment inputs straight out of its records: for pipelines and wells licensed by the AER 'the assessment must reflect the characteristics and specifications as of October 31 of the assessment year, as contained in the records of the AER'. Pipeline assessment classification codes are set by 'pipeline material, outside diameter, and the maximum operating pressure ... as contained in the records of the AER', and well depth is taken field by field — 'Total depth (field WELL-TOTAL-DEPTH of AER General Well File record type 010)', 'Deepest shoe set depth (field SHOE-SET-DEPTH of AER General Well File record type 040)', plug tops from record type 055. The guidelines also rely on the AER Insolvency List.
results.evidenceQuote: Total depth (field WELL-TOTAL-DEPTH of AER General Well File record type 010)

targetReport.title: AER General Well Data Report (General Well File)
targetReport.description: The Alberta Energy Regulator's authoritative record of every oil, gas, oil sands and water well licensed in Alberta, updated daily and distributed as fixed-format record types carrying licence number, well status, total depth, shoe set depth, plug intervals, material and operating pressure. It is the master register the province's regulated well and pipeline assessment reads from.
targetReport.cadence_note: Continuously maintained and updated daily; assessment freezes it at October 31 of the assessment year.

targetReport.title: Quarterly Production Survey in Manufacturing, Mining and Quarrying
targetReport.description: EVAS register no. 42131, listed in the GNI inventory's Chapter 10 table as a production- and expenditure-approach source, one of a family of items surveys covering manufacturing/mining/quarrying (alongside the cost structure survey, EVAS 42251, and the investment survey, EVAS 42231). Named directly in Chapter 6's discussion of output calculation: 'Production statistics by products and industries (EVAS 42131)'. CORRECTION 2026-08-09 (EU/G.74.md): domains was ['manufacturing'], which is not a member of the Domain union and never has been — the sole such value corpus-wide, undetected because nothing outside types.ts reads the field. Retagged 'national-accounts', which is the corpus's own convention for a production or manufacturing survey feeding the accounts (statcan-msm, statcan-asml, nl-cbs-sbs, au-abs-australian-industry all carry it) and is what this record's own description says it is — a GNI-inventory production- and expenditure-approach source. No new Domain member was minted: one node is not evidence that the union is missing a category, and 'manufacturing' as used here is the survey's subject matter rather than an economic domain in this field's sense. Nothing about the survey itself is corrected; the original description above is unchanged.
targetReport.cadence_note: Cadence stated in the survey's own title as given in the GNI inventory's Chapter 10 table ('Quarterly production survey'); not independently re-verified on a separate Destatis genesis-online page this session.

Q1 2026 results (ending 2026-03-31) would have been due by roughly 2026-07-15, which has already passed relative to today (2026-08-11); the next unreleased quarter is Q2 2026, due by roughly 2026-10-15. The City is now running the 2027-2030 Business Plans and Budgets process (community engagement in early-mid 2026, base budget to Council in May 2026, early review in July 2026), with the newsroom explicitly stating Council 'will develop and approve the 2027-2030 Business Plans and Budgets in November' 2026, continuing the same annual Nov/Dec pattern. results.basis: The 2026-29 Fiscal Plan (Budget 2026) is where the new disability assistance rate structure is set out: 'On July 1, 2026, the new Alberta Disability Assistance Program (ADAP) will start ... The maximum ADAP benefit rate will be set at $1,740 per month. Clients who transition from AISH to ADAP will receive a transition benefit of $200 per month, maintaining the maximum total benefit at the same level as AISH until December 31, 2027. As with AISH, ADAP benefit rates will be subject to the Alberta escalator policy annually, and former ADAP clients will continue to receive ongoing health benefits until age 65, regardless of employment income.' The Budget therefore sets the starting level that the escalator subsequently indexes.

results.basis: IMF Country Report No. 24/290 (Uganda: Staff Report for the 2024 Article IV Consultation, Informational Annex), Annex V 'Data Issues', Table 2: 'Uganda participates in the Enhanced General Data Dissemination System (e-GDDS) and publishes the data on its National Summary Data Page since November 2016.' Corroborated structurally by the IMF's own DSBB e-GDDS participants list (which includes Uganda) and its SDDS subscriber list (which does not). Reuses the imf-e-gdds node, placing Uganda on the same weaker dissemination tier already confirmed for Kenya, Nigeria, Ethiopia and Ghana, rather than the stronger SDDS tier confirmed for South Africa, Egypt and Tanzania.

targetReport.title: IMF Enhanced General Data Dissemination System (e-GDDS)
targetReport.description: The IMF's data-dissemination tier for countries not on the (stricter) SDDS/SDDS Plus standards already in the graph. Kenya implemented e-GDDS (with a National Summary Data Page) around 2018, per the IMF's own DSBB e-GDDS pages and confirmed via a related IMF press release. A notch below South Africa and Egypt, both confirmed on full SDDS -- worth having as a distinct node so the graph can actually show the tiering rather than treating every country's IMF dissemination status as equivalent.
targetReport.cadence_note: Standard itself revised rarely; not an annual release, matching the treatment given to imf-sdds.
